sections.footer: Source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Population change in the City of London in 2032

The population in the City of London is projected to increase from 11,457 people in 2022 to 17,023 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 13,960 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in the City of London
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In the City of London, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 798, with 1,478 births and 680 deaths in the City of London between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in the City of London by 7.0%, compared with an increase of 6.0% in London and an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 9,345, with 14,116 people moving to the area and 23,461 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in the City of London by 81.6%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to increase the population by 104, with 425 people moving to the area and 320 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in the City of London by 0.9%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 13,960, with 21,446 people moving to the area and 7,487 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in the City of London by 121.8%, compared with an increase of 14.7% in London and an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Age profile in the City of London in 2032

The median age in the City of London is projected to remain the same at 33 years between 2022 and 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 9% of the population in the City of London are projected to be aged 65 years or over, down from 11% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in the City of London between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in the City of London is projected to stay the same, at around 82%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to fall from 128 to 99 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in the City of London?

In 2032, 11% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, up from 8% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in the City of London between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will rise from 2% to 3%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will rise from 3% to 4%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 4%
